frequency_question: How often do highly contested Senate voting reform bills successfully overcome the 60-vote cloture threshold to pass?
membership_rule: Federal bills specifically targeting voter eligibility, registration procedures, or election administration that faced strict partisan polarization and required 60 votes to break a filibuster between 2005 and 2026.

cases.name: Help America Vote Act amendments / related integrity riders (2006)
Freedom to Vote Act / For the People Act (2021)
American Confidence in Elections Act style Senate companion attempts (2024)

provenance_note: rate of 0% from only 5 case(s); too few to establish an extreme base rate -- treat as directional
coverage_note: 5 major partisan voting/election integrity procedural showdowns identified; all failed to clear the 60-vote structural Senate friction point.
known_gaps: Minor non-controversial amendments or unanimous consent provisions are excluded because the target question concerns a highly contested structural partisan mandate.
skeleton: Not applicable; enumerated individual major partisan voting legislation attempts requiring 60 votes in the Senate over the specified period.
validity_reason: Valid until the expiration of the current Senate procedural rules (specifically the 60-vote filibuster threshold for legislation), which resets or faces potential reform at the start of each new Congress.
